ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended (AML/CFT Act); Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE) (Loi du 13 janvier 2019 sur le registre des bénéficiaires effectifs), transposing Directive (EU) 2015/849 and Directive (EU) 2018/843; Grand-Ducal Regulation of 1 February 2019 on the practical operation of the RBE; CSSF Regulation No 12-02 of 14 December 2012 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended; Law of 27 October 2010 on fiduciary contracts and on similar institutions; Luxembourg Criminal Code Articles on money laundering and terrorist financing; and the amended Law of 28 July 2020 implementing the ECJ ruling in Case C-37/20 restricting public access to beneficial ownership information to competent authorities and persons with a legitimate interest.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory enhanced due diligence screening of all UBOs, directors, managers, and authorized signatories against the Luxembourg national PEP list, EU consolidated financial sanctions list (EU Council Regulation simplified screening), OFAC SDN list, UN Security Council consolidated list, INTERPOL notices, and domestic judicial sanctions databases. Screening must be conducted prior to notarization and repeated within 5 business days before signing the deed of incorporation. Results must be documented in a compliance memorandum retained for at least 5 years.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) via the Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) portal at www.lbr.lu
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names may be expressed in any language but must be composed of Latin script characters and be capable of transcription into the national alphabet. The name must include the legal form sector 'SARL' or 'Société à Responsabilité Limitée'. The name must be clearly distinguishable from all existing RCS-registered names and must not be misleading as to the company's activity, nationality, or public authority affiliation. Foreign-script names require a sworn transliteration and translation into French or German; a single official variant is registered. Trade names (enseignes) may differ from the corporate name but must comply with the same distinctiveness rules.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection of a proposed name by the Luxembourg Business Registers, the applicant must first obtain a written statement of grounds from the RCS. An administrative appeal may be filed with the Ministry of Justice within 15 days from notification of the rejection, supported by legal argumentation establishing distinctiveness and non-misleading character. If the administrative appeal is unsuccessful, a judicial remedy is available before the Tribunal Administratif within 3 months from the administrative decision. A new name reservation application may be submitted concurrently; each reservation is valid for 30 days and may be renewed once upon request.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or domiciliation address is permissible solely for registered-office purposes provided the domiciliation agent is a duly licensed professional domiciliation company that maintains an actual physical premises in Luxembourg. For the target revenue-based financing fund activity, the annual Report on Administrative and Economic Substance and the substance rules for financing undertakings require genuine decision-making, core business activity, and operational staff in Luxembourg. A mere virtual mailbox without operational substance is not permissible; the Luxembourg tax administration may deem the registered office fictitious and impose penalties.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk of unannounced physical on-site inspections is 20% per annum within the first two fiscal years, increasing to 35% for entities using domiciliation services without demonstrated local substance. Inspections may be conducted by the CSSF (financial monitoring), the Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AED), and the RBE competent authorities.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended, Articles 710-1 et seq. governing the Société à Responsabilité Limitée (SARL); complemented by the Law of 19 December 2019 on the Register of Commerce and Companies (RCS) and the Law of 13 January 2019 on the establishment of the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) electronic filing framework
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés – RCS), operated by the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) under the Ministry of Justice
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Acte constitutif (Notarial Deed of Incorporation containing the Articles of Association/Statuts), filed electronically via the e-RCS portal of the Luxembourg Business Registers
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum subscribed share capital of EUR 12,000 (fully subscribed at incorporation); at least 25% of each cash contribution, i.e. a minimum of EUR 3,000, must be paid up at signing; in-kind contributions must be fully paid up at incorporation; payment is evidenced by a Luxembourg bank blocking certificate (attestation de blocage) or a notary-held escrow certificate; no mandatory long-term escrow account is required after RCS registration
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the shareholders of the Société à Responsabilité Limitée, acting unanimously at this first meeting, do hereby: 1. SUBSCRIBE in full to the company's share capital of EUR 12,000, representing [X] shares at EUR [Y] each; the subscribed capital is paid up in accordance with the bank blocking certificate issued by [Bank]. 2. ADOPT as registered office the premises at [Address], Grand Duchy of Luxembourg, effective upon RCS registration. 3. APPOINT [Name] as manager (gérant) with full powers to represent the company, acting singly, and [Name] as alternate signatory. 4. INSTRUCT the notary to execute the deed of incorporation, complete RCS registration, and commence the establishment permit application. This resolution is effective immediately and until revoked.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate name reservation and negative clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) via e-RCS online portal and MyGuichet.lu
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Search the RCS database to confirm availability, reserve the proposed corporate name, and request a negative certificate (certificat de non-confusion). The SARL name must include or be accompanied by the words 'Société à Responsabilité Limitée' or the abbreviation 'SARL'. Retain the negative certificate for the notary and bank file.
required_dossiers: Name reservation application
Passport or national ID of each subscribing shareholder
Consent of the proposed manager (gérant) to serve
Draft articles of association (statuts)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused due to identity or confusion with an existing entity, file a modified name request with a new negative certificate; appeal to the RCS within one month of refusal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank account opening and capital blocking certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg credit institution (bank) selected by the incorporators
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary blocked account in the name of the SARL in formation with a Luxembourg bank. Deposit the minimum paid-up share capital (at least EUR 3,000 cash, or 100% of any in-kind contribution). Instruct the bank to issue a blocking certificate (attestation de blocage) addressed to the notary confirming that the funds are irrevocably blocked until the company has been registered with the RCS.
required_dossiers: Negative certificate from RCS
Draft articles of association
Passport or national ID of shareholders and managers
Proof of residential address of officers
Bank KYC forms, source of funds declaration, and beneficial ownership identification
Preliminary business plan confirming activity under ISIC 6499
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses KYC clearance or delays the blocking certificate, submit enhanced source-of-funds documentation, select an alternative Luxembourg bank, or use the notary's escrow account for capital blocking and provide the notary escrow certificate instead.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the notarial deed of incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg notary (Notaire) in the district of the registered office; Chamber of Notaries of Luxembourg
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The notary reviews the draft statuts and the bank blocking certificate, verifies the identity and capacity of all subscribing shareholders and of the manager(s), and authenticates the deed of incorporation. All shareholders must appear before the notary or be validly represented by a notarised power of attorney. If contributions in kind are made, they must be fully paid up and described in the deed. Upon signature, the shares are fully subscribed and the company acquires provisional legal existence pending RCS registration.
required_dossiers: RCS negative certificate
Bank blocking certificate (attestation de blocage)
Draft articles of association (statuts)
Passport or national ID of each shareholder and manager
Certificate of non-conviction (extrait du casier judiciaire – bulletin n°3) for each manager
Power of attorney if a shareholder is represented
Valuation report for any in-kind contribution
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies deficiencies in the statuts or the capital evidence, amend the statuts by rider, obtain a corrected blocking certificate, and re-sign the deed before the same notary without loss of priority.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (e-RCS filing)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The notary files the authenticated deed of incorporation electronically via the e-RCS portal within one month of signature. The filing includes the statutory forms on directors, managers, and beneficial owners. Upon approval, the RCS assigns the company's registration number (RCS number) and the company acquires separate legal personality. The RCS extracts are then publicly available.
required_dossiers: Notarial deed of incorporation
Bank blocking certificate
Identity forms for managers (formulaire de renseignements)
Beneficial owner declaration (registre des bénéficiaires effectifs – RBE form)
Statement of acceptance by each manager
Proof of payment of the RCS filing fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues a query or requests supplementary documents, cure the deficiency within 15 days by filing the missing exhibit electronically; if the filing is rejected, the notary re-submits a corrected file and the effective registration date is the date of the new successful deposit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication in the Official Electronic Gazette (RESA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: RCS / Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Following RCS registration, the register automatically publishes the statutory excerpts of the incorporation (company name, form, registered office, object, capital, officers) in RESA, which constitutes the mandatory third-party notice. No separate application by the company is required; the publication occurs electronically and is free of charge.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RESA publication contains errors, file a request for rectification with the RCS and obtain a corrected publication; third parties may rely on the original publication until corrected.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Establishment permit, tax registration, VAT, and social security enrolment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of the Economy (Guichet des Entreprises via MyGuichet.lu); Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD); Administration de l'Enregistrement, des Domaines et de la TVA; Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS); optional notification to the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) only if structured as an alternative investment fund, which is not required for the present royalty financing mandate
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the application for the general business establishment permit (autorisation d'établissement) for the manager and for the company via MyGuichet.lu, attesting the professional qualification and good conduct of the manager. Register the company with the ACD for corporate income tax, municipal business tax, and net wealth tax; register for VAT if the financing activity generates taxable supplies; and enrol the manager and any employees with CCSS for social security. Because the business is an unregulated non-dilutive revenue-based financing fund under ISIC 6499, no CSSF banking licence is required; however, verify eligibility for any self-declared AIF regime.
required_dossiers: RCS registration extract
Deed of incorporation and statuts
Criminal record record (bulletin n°3) of the manager
Proof of professional qualification or management experience
Lease agreement for the registered office
Tax registration form (formulaire RC – renseignements concernant la société)
VAT registration form (formulaire 1 TVA)
Social security enrolment form (LS/SS)
Sworn statement of the manager for the establishment permit
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the establishment permit is refused or queried, submit supplementary evidence of qualifications or amend the corporate object to exclude regulated activities; appeal the Ministry's decision before the administrative courts within three months; for tax or VAT registration queries, provide the requested documentation directly to the relevant administration within 15 days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of the Economy – Direction Générale des Classes Moyennes (business establishment permit); commune of the registered office for physical premises; Notification to CSSF only in the optional event of AIF structuring, not required for the present unregulated royalty financing activity
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorisation d'établissement (Business Establishment Permit) issued to the SARL and its managing officer for the pursuit of commercial activities under ISIC 6499; no separate financial-sector licence is required for royalty-based financing activities conducted with proprietary funds

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'Environnement (Luxembourg Environmental Protection Agency), under the Ministry of the Environment, Climate and Biodiversity; local municipal environmental service for sewer and waste matters
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – Full EIA Not Required: the activity is a tertiary-sector financial services office with no industrial installation listed under the Luxembourg law on classified establishments (établissements classés), therefore only a simple municipal occupancy notice and waste-management compliance apply
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process wastewater, VOC, or combustion emissions generated; sanitary wastewater must comply with municipal sewer discharge rules and the general wastewater regulations of the Water Management Administration; office waste must be selectively sorted and disposed of in accordance with the Law of 9 June 2022 on waste prevention and management; any IT equipment waste must be transferred to an authorised e-waste scheme; noise levels limited to communal urban-planning thresholds

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification (attestation de sécurité incendie) issued by the municipal fire prevention service and the Grand-Ducal Fire and Rescue Corps (CGDIS) for the registered office; structural load inspection and building occupancy certificate from the municipal building authority; workplace health and safety clearance from the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM), covering ergonomic workstations, electrical safety, evacuation signage, first-aid equipment, and compliance with OSH standards equivalent to the European framework.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for corporate income tax and Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT; unified corporate registration through Luxembourg Business Registers (RCSL) portal (https://www.lbr.lu) and eCDF tax filing portal (https://ecdf.public.lu)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a Luxembourg SARL, the statutory procedure is: (1) execute the incorporation deed before a Luxembourg notary and file the articles of association with the Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS); (2) obtain the national identification number (numéro d'identification / matricule) assigned by the RCSL; (3) register for VAT with the AEDT by filing the VAT registration form via MyGuichet to obtain a Luxembourg VAT number (LU + 8 digits); (4) the ACD automatically registers the company for corporate income tax and municipal business tax upon RCS filing; non-resident entities without a Luxembourg establishment that have a direct tax liability or VAT taxable event must register directly with the AEDT/ACD and, if VAT-liable in Luxembourg, may be required to appoint a local tax representative.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation (resident SARL is a taxable company subject to Luxembourg corporate income tax, municipal business tax, and net wealth tax on a worldwide basis, subject to participation exemption, IP box, and permanent establishment exemptions; no tax-exempt zone regime applies)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg does not have a US-style check-the-box election. Available statutory elections include: (i) fiscal unity (tax consolidation) election under article 164bis LIR for resident companies that hold at least 99% of the subsidiary's capital and voting rights; (ii) hybrid mismatch re-characterisation elections under the ATAD implementation, including options to align payment treatment for interest restriction and controlled foreign company rules; (iii) the option for securitisation vehicles to ring-fence assets and liabilities under the Securitisation Law; (iv) election to apply the IP box regime for qualifying intellectual property income at 80% exemption; (v) VAT grouping is available under specific conditions for Luxembourg-established VAT taxable persons.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée, TVA) harmonised with the EU VAT Directive 2006/112/EC
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 annual taxable turnover threshold for the small-enterprise franchise regime under Article 57a of the Luxembourg VAT Statute; non-resident taxable persons supplying goods or services in Luxembourg are required to register for VAT without any threshold, unless a special EU scheme applies (e.g., One Stop Shop).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time continuous transaction controls (CTC), digital stamping, or fiscal clearance mechanism is currently enacted for Luxembourg domestic B2B invoicing. Mandatory electronic invoicing applies only to public procurement invoices issued to Luxembourg public authorities, which must be submitted through the Luxembourg e-Procurement platform in PEPPOL BIS format. VAT returns, recapitulative statements, and Intrastat filings must be submitted electronically via eCDF/MyGuichet; tax clearance is performed ex-post through periodic VAT audits and risk-based inspection.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating is available for: (i) exports of goods physically sent to a destination outside the European Union, provided the supplier holds sufficient documentary evidence of dispatch and transport; (ii) services supplied to a customer established outside the EU where the place-of-supply rules allocate the supply to the third-country destination; (iii) certain international transport and related services. For the royalty financing fund, financial services are generally exempt without credit and not zero-rated; zero-rating may be claimed only for ancillary services (e.g., advisory fees, collection agency services) that qualify as B2B services supplied to non-EU counterparties under the place-of-supply rules.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: EU Single Administrative Document (SAD) / Customs Export Declaration
Signed Bill of Lading (B/L) or CMR transport waybill
Inward Remittance Certificate issued by the receiving bank or bank statement showing foreign currency settlement
Proof of ownership transfer and transport insurance documents
SWIFT MT103 or equivalent wire transfer evidence
Foreign exchange conversion confirmation, if applicable
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Luxembourg tax authorities may reassess zero-rated supplies retrospectively if export evidence is deficient, and are entitled to claw back input VAT together with interest at 0.8% per month and administrative fines ranging from 5% to 100% of the VAT understated. Fraudulent zero-rating claims, including falsified export documentation or artificial circular transaction structures, constitute tax fraud ( escroquerie fiscale) and are punishable by imprisonment of up to five years and fines up to €500,000, as well as forfeiture of deductibility and solidary liability for company directors and representatives.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), together with the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) for bank licensing and AML/CTF supervision; Luxembourg operates within the Eurosystem and settles large-value euro payments via the ECB's TARGET2 platform.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg maintains fully liberalised capital and current account movements under TFEU Article 63 and the EU's free movement of capital acquis. The euro is fully convertible with no exchange controls, no BCL pre-authorisation for cross-border flows, and no restrictions on profit or dividend remittance. Fiscal hurdles only: 15% Luxembourg dividend withholding tax may apply on distributions, but is eliminated under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive (0% for qualifying 10% shareholdings) or reduced under double tax treaties; non-profit-linked interest payments to non-resident lenders are exempt from withholding tax, while IP royalties are subject to 15% WHT unless exempt under the EU Interest & Royalties Directive (2003/49/EC) or an applicable DTT. Balance-of-payments statistical reporting obligations rest on the banking counterparties, not on the SARL.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None applicable. The Eurosystem and Luxembourg law impose no surrender, mandatory conversion, or repatriation timeline on export proceeds. Export receipts in EUR or any freely convertible foreign currency may be held offshore or onshore without BCL approval; only the collecting bank's statistical BOP reporting applies.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (Spuerkeess/BCEE)

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Multi-Currency Account + Capital Escrow Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium-Low. CSSF-authorised payment institutions or EMIs (e.g., MANGOPAY S.A., EDEA PAY S.A.) may operate only as segregated collection rails for royalty receipts via SEPA Direct Debit and card pay-ins; they may not grant commercial credit, hold the SARL's financing capital as escrow, or execute FX forwards under the Law of 10 November 2009 on payment services. EU passported digital banks/EMIs (e.g., Qonto, Bunq) can serve as secondary operating accounts for day-to-day expenses but are unsuitable as the primary treasury bank for a lending-like royalty financing vehicle. A full Luxembourg or EU credit institution remains mandatory for treasury, lending disbursements, and hedging.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Luxembourg AML law (Law of 12 November 2004, as amended) does not impose an absolute statutory requirement for directors or UBOs to appear physically before the bank; remote identification via qualified video-KYC and eIDAS-compliant electronic signatures is legally possible. In practice, however, leading Luxembourg banks require at least one onboarding interview (physical or video) with the managing director, and may demand a physical visit for UBOs resident in non-EU high-risk jurisdictions. Remote account opening is feasible where the bank accepts certified corporate documents, a power of attorney, and verified board resolutions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: SARL classified as an 'Investment Entity' under CRS/AEOI, with layered offshore (e.g., Cayman) ownership creating source-of-funds opacity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Luxembourg RBE (Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs) certificate; notarised ownership chain and register of shareholders; CRS self-certification and tax residence certificates for all UBOs; audited board resolution appointing a CRS reporting officer; corporate chart and organisational structure signed by a Luxembourg legal advisor.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: ISIC 6499 revenue-based financing may be assessed as unlicensed lending or deposit-taking under the Law of 5 April 1993 on the financial sector.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Legal opinion from a Luxembourg law firm confirming the private-lending exclusion for own-funds financing; evidence that no repayable funds are accepted from the public; contractual precedent of royalty purchase agreements; audited cash-flow model showing own-capital deployment; CSSF declinature letter, if obtained, or a non-regulated-status memorandum.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: high-volume, low-ticket ACH/direct-debit receipts from hundreds of digital merchants, resembling payment intermediation rather than a financing fund.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Master financing agreements and revenue-share schedules; merchant on-boarding and KYC file for each counterparty above EUR 10,000 exposure; ERP-generated reconciliation of disbursements vs royalty receipts; treasury policy confirming the SARL is the principal, not agent; sample invoices and collection reports.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: rapid round-tripping where inbound capital injection is disbursed within 48 hours to merchants in FATF-monitored or sanctions-sensitive jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Daily liquidity forecast and board-approved disbursement policy with dual signature; source-of-wealth documentation of the shareholder (bank statements, subscription agreement, capital call notice); negative screening report for sanctions, PEPs, and adverse media; contractual nexus for each high-risk counterparty; TARGET2/SEPA settlement evidence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: CRS/FATCA reporting failure risk if the SARL holds accounts for third parties or fails its own financial institution classification.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Completed CRS/FATCA self-certification forms; classification memo confirming the entity's status (Non-Reporting Financial Institution if applicable); testimonial of local tax counsel; up-to-date RBE declaration; evidence of filing through the Luxembourg ACD portal where required.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity capital from shareholders must be wired via SWIFT MT103 (non-SEPA) or SEPA Credit Transfer in EUR to the SARL's IBAN at the receiving Luxembourg credit institution. The payment must carry an ISO 20022 purpose code such as 'EQUI' for equity subscription or 'LOAN' for intercompany shareholder loans; the receiving bank will map this to the ECB/BOP category for direct investment or other investment-loans for BCL statistical reporting. Remittance fields must quote the notarial capital-increase deed date and notary reference, the SARL's RCS number, and the share premium account. The bank will require a certified copy of the notarial deed of capital increase, the updated extract of the RCS, and the RBE filing confirmation before final credit. For a capital increase, the contribution must be fully paid into a Luxembourg bank account or a blocked escrow referenced in the deed; MT202 COV should be avoided unless the beneficiary detail in the cover payment exactly mirrors the SARL's legal name and IBAN.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Disbursements to supported digital brands within the EEA are executed via SEPA Credit Transfer (SCT) or SEPA Instant; non-EEA and non-EUR payouts use SWIFT MT103 with field 70 referencing the disbursement contract and underlying revenue-sharing agreement. USD, GBP, and CHF outflows clear through Fedwire/CHIPS, CHAPS, and SIX via the Luxembourg bank's correspondent network. Commercial Letters of Credit (UCP 600) are available where trade collateral exists but are non-standard for royalty financing; the primary rail is a clean MT103 transfer. Collections from merchants are best structured as SEPA Direct Debit B2B mandates routed to a dedicated EMI or collection account, then swept daily via SEPA into the treasury account. Disbursements above EUR 50,000 to non-EEA beneficiaries require dual executive signature and prior AML committee clearance; all payouts must be backed by an approved disbursement schedule retained in the audit trail.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable EUR/USD, EUR/GBP and EUR/CHF outright forwards under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement with the relationship bank
FX swaps (spot-forward and forward-forward) for rolling short-term EUR/USD exposure from royalty collections
Cross-currency swaps to convert USD-denominated financing assets into EUR for balance-sheet matching
European-style FX options (purchased only, no naked writing) to cap the conversion cost of expected non-EUR revenue shares
EURIBOR/EUROSTR interest-rate swaps, caps, and floors to hedge floating-rate exposure inherent in the revenue-based financing book

NDFs are unavailable for EUR given full convertibility; NDFs for exotic disbursement currencies (e.g., BRL, TRY) are permissible only through a global prime broker with fully documented underlying transactions

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts deposit (comptes annuels) — balance sheet, profit and loss statement, and notes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCSL / Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 months after financial year-end; for a calendar-year SARL, by 31 July of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Court-ordered coercive fines (astreinte) for non-filing; directors' civil liability for damages; repeated failure over two years may lead to judicial winding-up or administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial owner register declaration or update (RBE / Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners, operated by the RCSL
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after any share transfer, change in voting rights, or change in control; no separate annual filing is due if no change occurs in the year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal fine up to EUR 125,000 and imprisonment up to 6 months for deliberate non-disclosure; possible suspension of voting rights and refusal of notarial acts for incomplete records.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax / net wealth tax return (CIT-IFT return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg direct tax authority (Administration des contributions directes, ACD)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For financial year ending 31 December N, return must be filed by 30 June N+1 in electronic form (paper filing by 31 May N+1); extensions may be granted on request
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing surcharge of 10% of assessed taxes; monthly interest of 0.6% on unpaid tax; criminal prosecution for intentional failure to file.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory audit for a SARL if at least two of three criteria are exceeded for two consecutive years: total balance sheet EUR 4.4 million, net turnover EUR 8.8 million, average workforce 50; no audit is required below these thresholds unless parent-company rules, public-interest status, or statutes require.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP under the amended Law of 10 August 1915 and the accounting directive 2013/34/EU; IFRS permitted for consolidated accounts and voluntary for unlisted single-entity financial statements in certain situations.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Luxembourg does not impose a separate annual UBO confirmation filing. However, the RBE must be updated within one month of every share transfer or beneficial-ownership change, and the board must review the file at least annually at the balance-sheet date to ensure it reflects current ownership.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 17% Luxembourg corporate income tax (IRC) above EUR 175,000 taxable profit, plus 7% solidarity surcharge on the IRC; municipalities levy an additional municipal business tax (impôt commercial communal) at rates between 6.75% and 12.64%. The aggregate statutory headline rate in Luxembourg City is approximately 24.94%.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Luxembourg IP Box: 80% exemption for qualifying IP income, producing an effective rate of approximately 5%. Participation exemption: 100% exemption for qualifying dividend income and capital gains. 5-year initial-loss continuity safe harbour; general carryforward of unused tax losses remains available in subsequent years.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulaire 750 (annual corporate income tax and municipal business tax declaration) filed electronically via MyGuichet.lu, the Luxembourg single digital gateway operated by the Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual. Quarterly provisional instalments for corporate income tax and municipal business tax are due where the taxpayer has an existing tax assessment; the annual return reconciles all instalments.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual return must be filed by 30 June of the calendar year immediately following the fiscal year-end. For a 31 December year-end, the statutory deadline is 30 June. Approved tax advisers may request extensions through the electronic portal.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, RCS Luxembourg registration number, registered office, Luxembourg tax file number, ISIC/NAF code, legal form, and status of the taxpayer as a resident SARL or a Luxembourg permanent establishment of a foreign company.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident companies complete this section only to identify the name of the Luxembourg permanent establishment and its Luxembourg tax file number; pure licensor or financing entities without a Luxembourg PE should not open a Form 750.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Form 750, Section 2 – Determination of taxable result
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Entry of commercial net profit from audited or certified financial statements, followed by tax adjustments for non-deductible expenses, depreciation recapture, hidden distributions, interest limitation, royalty and financing revenues, and reversal or addition of tax-exempt income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents input only income and expenses economically attributable to the Luxembourg PE. Outbound royalties and interest received by a non-resident with no PE are normally outside Luxembourg CIT and are not entered.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Form 750, Section 3 – Tax incentives and deductions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: IP Box deduction (80% of qualifying IP income), participation exemption for dividends and capital gains, notional interest deduction, investment tax credits, and territorial or PE exemption claims. Attach schedules and supporting documentation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: IP Box and participation exemption are generally available only to Luxembourg resident taxpayers or Luxembourg PEs; a non-resident without a PE cannot claim these provisions on the Form 750.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax losses incurred in prior years and available for set-off against current taxable profit, subject to the continuity-of-activity condition and the relevant carryforward schedule.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only losses attributable to the Luxembourg PE of a non-resident may be entered; foreign losses of the head office or other foreign PEs are not deductible in Luxembourg.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Form 750, Summary and computation of tax
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total taxable income, application of 17% IRC rate and solidarity surcharge, municipal business tax allocation by commune, and deduction of advance payments or foreign tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents with a Luxembourg PE complete the summary only for the PE; municipal tax allocation is confined to the commune in which the PE is situated.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing after formal notice can trigger an administrative penalty up to 10% of assessed tax, plus monthly arrears interest of 0.6%. Best-judgment assessment is made when no return is filed. Deliberate false filing constitutes tax fraud, subject to criminal fines, imprisonment up to 5 years, and surcharges up to 100% of evaded tax.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% on gross dividends distributed by a Luxembourg SARL to non-resident shareholders. The rate is 0% for qualifying corporate shareholders under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive or the domestic participation exemption, and may be reduced to 0%-15% under applicable double tax treaties.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To obtain treaty relief before distribution, the non-resident beneficial owner must provide the Luxembourg paying agent with a valid tax residency certificate (TRC) issued by its residence state, a beneficial ownership declaration, and, where the treaty contains a limitation-on-benefits or principal purpose test, evidence of economic substance. The paying agent retains the documents and applies the treaty zero rate. If tax was withheld at source, the beneficial owner may file a refund claim with the Luxembourg tax administration within the applicable statutory limitation period.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Luxembourg imposes no domestic withholding tax on outbound interest or royalty payments made to non-residents. The EU Interest-Royalty Directive also eliminates any withholding tax on interest and royalties between associated EU companies. Most Luxembourg tax treaties provide for 0% withholding on interest and 0% or 5% on royalties. Payments of such income to a Luxembourg permanent establishment remain subject to Luxembourg corporate income tax.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Master File required where the multinational group consolidated revenue equals or exceeds EUR 50,000,000. Local File required for a Luxembourg entity when its aggregate related-party transactions in a relevant category exceed EUR 2,500,000, or when the Luxembourg entity itself is significant within the group. Country-by-Country Report filing applies to groups with consolidated revenue of at least EUR 750,000,000.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg does not have separate Economic Substance Regulations comparable to offshore ESR regimes, but substance requirements are embedded in Art. 56 LIR, judicial anti-abuse doctrines, ATAD general anti-abuse rules, and treaty limitation-on-benefits analysis. A Luxembourg SARL engaged in royalty financing and fund activities must demonstrate local substance including board control, senior management, staff, office premises, risk management, and actual economic ownership of the financial and IP assets; otherwise tax deductions, treaty benefits, and Luxembourg tax residence may be denied.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax evasion and fraudulent corporate income tax filing
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Understating revenue-based financing income, fabricating deductible royalty expenses, backdating loan or financing agreements, submitting forged tax residence certificates, or failing to file the Form 750 after formal notice while continuing to operate.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Best-judgment tax assessment, 0.6% monthly arrears interest, fraud surcharges up to 100% of the evaded tax, criminal fines, and imprisonment up to 5 years. The tax administration may also publish the judgment and disqualify the company from public contracts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false declarations or knowingly cause the company to evade taxes are jointly and severally liable for the resulting tax, interest, and penalties. Criminal courts may impose imprisonment, fines, asset seizure, and exit or travel bans. Civil liability under Luxembourg principles of faute de gestion permits creditors or the tax administration to pursue personal claims against directors.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Abusive shell company and artificial royalty/financing structure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a Luxembourg SARL as a letterbox company that merely circulates royalty or revenue-based financing payments, with no local employees, no board meetings, no local bank account, no local risk decisions, and with all substantive functions performed abroad solely to obtain Luxembourg tax or treaty benefits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Disallowance of deductions, recharacterisation of royalty payments as dividends or hidden equity distributions, imposition of Luxembourg dividend withholding tax up to 15% on the recharacterised amount, denial of treaty benefits under the principal purpose test, and application of ATAD CFC rules attributing income to the controlling shareholder.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Where the corporate form is a pure façade or the directors knowingly participate in an abusive circular arrangement, courts may pierce the corporate veil and hold the directors personally responsible for unpaid taxes and restitution. Travel bans and criminal sanctions may apply where fraudulent intent is established.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer pricing non-compliance and documentation failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Setting intercompany royalty rates or revenue-based financing yields outside the arm’s length range, failing to prepare and maintain a Local File or Master File despite the EUR 50,000,000 group threshold or EUR 2,500,000 related-party transaction threshold, and producing inconsistent or fabricated functional analyses.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax adjustment under Art. 56 LIR to a deemed arm’s length profit, revocation of deductions for excessive payments, 0.6% monthly arrears interest, and general penalties applicable to understated income. Deliberate documentation falsification escalates the case to criminal tax fraud proceedings.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors responsible for approving non-arm’s length pricing and for destroying or manufacturing TP documentation may become personally liable for the tax deficiency and for damages to the company. Criminal sanctions include imprisonment and fines for forgery and tax fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML, UBO register non-compliance, and unlicensed financial activity
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentionally concealing the real beneficial owner of the Luxembourg SARL in the Register of Beneficial Owners, financing customers with tainted funds, failing to apply AML/KYC controls, or operating a revenue-based financing scheme that publicly invites funds without the licence required by Luxembourg financial law.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The UBO register omission exposes the company and its managers to administrative fines. Money laundering constitutes a criminal offence under the Luxembourg Criminal Code, carrying imprisonment of up to 5 years and fines reaching the value of the laundered assets. Unregulated financial activity may trigger CSSF enforcement, asset freezing, and compulsory dissolution.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are criminally liable for money laundering if they knowingly process illicit proceeds; civil restitution orders, confiscation of assets, travel bans, and disqualification from holding managerial office may be imposed even where the SARL’s liability is limited.
